item.title: After historic outing, Victor Wembanyama put focus on Mitch Johnson's 100th win
item.description: San Antonio Spurs Victor Wembanyama (1) gets congratulation from San Antonio Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson in a Spurs preseason opener vs. Guangzhou Loong-Lions on Monday, Oct. 6, 2025 at Frost Bank Center. (Ronald Cortes) PORTLAND, Ore. - Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama left the court with the game ball in his large hands after his magnificent, history-making performance in Wednesday's 112-111 victory over Dallas. He didn't keep it long, though. Rather than take the ball home as a cherished keepsake from his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block masterpiece, the 22-year-old Frenchman presented it to Mitch Johnson in the locker room to honor him on the occasion of his 100th career coaching win. "I haven't checked the data, but it's got to be up there with one of the fastest hundred wins. We're all just proud of him and he deserves it," Wembanyama said after posting 30 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks to lead the Spurs to a 124-109 triumph over the Kings on Friday in Sacramento. Teammates applauded Wembanyama's unselfish gesture on a night he joined Wilt Chamberlain as the only NBA players to finish a game with 50-plus points, 20-plus rebounds and eight-plus blocks. "It just shows the type of person he is," Dylan Harper said. "A player of that stature could be very self-centered. He could be very to himself, but he pours into us and he pours into the team, the coaching staff, the whole organization. And that's a testament to how he grew up, his family and just who he is as a person." San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) prepares to walk off the court after a game against the Dallas Mavericks at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) had a career-high in scoring with 52 points. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Dallas Mavericks 112-111. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Johnson, 39, called the gift he received from Wembanyama "one of the many examples of how team-oriented" the 7-foot-4 center has been since he joined the Spurs as the No. 1 overall pick of the 2023 NBA Draft. "It can get lost at times with his talent and greatness and potential greatness and all the moments that are surrounded by individual accomplishments or moments he creates," the coach said. Johnson, who joined the Spurs as a G League assistant in 2016 before going on to serve on Hall of Famer Gregg Popovich's staff, became the Spurs acting head coach in November 2024 after Popovich suffered a stroke. After guiding the Spurs to a 32-45 record in a season filled with challenges, the club named Johnson head coach in May 2025 after Popovich, the NBA's all-time winningest coach, announced his retirement from coaching. The Spurs finished 62-20 last season before starting this season 7-2 after recording their seventh win in a row Friday. item.title: Penn State football injury issues at wide receiver vs Washington
item.description: SEATTLE — Penn State football appears to be getting healthy at most every place on its roster for the stretch drive, in order to best save whatever it can of a second straight disappointing season. To start by building momentum and positivity for its cross-country adventure here on Saturday, Nov. 7, in Washington's Husky Stadium . Getting healthy most everywhere except for their rebuilt receiver room. While senior Chase Sowell appears to be returning from injury against the Huskies , sophomore sensation Koby Howard will miss his sixth straight game with an undisclosed injury, according to the latest Big Ten availability report . Meanwhile, freshman wideout Zay Robinson was listed as "questionable" all week and will be a "game-time decision" against the Huskies. Robinson also has excelled as the Lions' primary kickoff and punt returner. Other game-time decisions include starting offensive tackle Malachi Goodman and top backup defensive tackle Armstrong Nnodim. This means the Lions' viable receiving options Saturday could be down to Sowell, junior transfer Brett Eskildsen and true freshman Amarion Jackson. Eskildsen, one of the fastest players on the team, is averaging only 30.5 yards per game on his 23 receptions this season. Rather, the Lions and quarterback Rocco Becht may lean, again, on their tight end room that finally appears fully healthy, particularly standout blocker and possession receiver Gabe Burkle, who has been working his way back from knee surgery last fall. Otherwise, the Lions appear in better shape, physically, for Washington and the final three games than they have for most of the season. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Washington game includes Howard, linebacker Alex Tatsch, defensive end Max Granville , cornerback Tyler Armstead, defensive tackle Alijah Carnell and kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa . item.title: Tuipulotu takes 'full responsibility' for Scotland collapse
item.description: Captain Sione Tuipulotu took responsibility for Scotland's second-half Nations Championship collapse against New Zealand, saying they were "nowhere near accurate enough". Trailing by just three points at half-time, Scotland were well in the contest as they sought a first victory against the All Blacks at the 34th attempt. However, they failed to score any points in the second half as New Zealand swept to a clinical 43-21 victory at Murrayfield. Tuipulotu was sin-binned on 50 minutes after a succession of penalties went against the Scots and they were unable to wrestle back momentum from there. "Disappointing," was Tuipulotu's one-word review post-match. He added: "We played our rugby in the first half but we probably left points out there. We were nowhere near accurate enough second half, and we couldn't stick with them, it's really disappointing. "Our discipline wasn't good enough, and it starts with me. I got sent to the bin and 10 minutes with your captain off isn't good for any team. I take full responsibility for that." New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade All the Scottish rugby latest in one place Scotland conceded 13 penalties to New Zealand's eight. Just moments after Tuipulotu went to the bin, Beauden Barrett cruised over to score his second and New Zealand's sixth try of the day. Game over. "First half we were playing our rugby, putting them under pressure with ball in hand, in a way they haven't been put under pressure over the past couple of weeks," Tuipulotu said. "We just weren't accurate enough when we got down into the 22m. We had lots of opportunities in the first half and weren't accurate enough in the second. "We know what we can do with ball in hand, which proves we weren't up to the level that the All Blacks were playing in the second half. "It's a must-win game [against Australia] next week, we'll regroup and stick together like we always do." In the first half, Scotland's maul and New Zealand's indiscipline kept the hosts in touch. After the interval, the All Blacks tightened up defensively and scored three magnificent tries. "Scotland kept getting the wrong side of Andrew Brace with Sione Tuiputotu going to the sin-bin," former Scotland captain John Barclay said on STV. "But the difference is red zone efficiency - when the team gets into the opposition 22m, how often do they score? New Zealand were at 58%, Scotland were at 30%. "There's a couple moments in the second half where they manage to get down into the 22m, and they lost the ball first phase. It's that clinical edge." item.title: Bryson DeChambeau Faces Hard Choice After LIV Collapse
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Bryson DeChambeau has until November 16 to secure a spot on the DP World Tour or lose his playing privileges. The two-time major winner faces a critical choice after LIV Golf announced it will liquidate operations. His five-year exemption, earned by winning the 2024 U.S. Open, will expire unless he acts now. This deadline comes just one day after the season-ending DP World Tour Championship concludes. The window to claim Category 1 status is closing fast for the world No. 38. LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September after its financial backer walked away. A $300 million rescue deal with BC Partners fell apart this week when the firm pulled out. The league told a New Jersey bankruptcy court on November 5 that it would abandon its restructuring plans. This decision leaves players like DeChambeau without a guaranteed home for the 2027 season. The collapse happened faster than many expected, including the players who stayed loyal to the league. The Cost of Confidence Just seven days ago, DeChambeau shared on a podcast his belief that the league possesses a bright future. He told ‘Figuring Out’ that “The business model makes a lot of sense.” He also stated, according to AOL.com , “This is going to be a league, hopefully, that exists forever.” Those words now sound like a miscalculation given the sudden liquidation. He never formally committed to the proposed “LIV 2.0” structure, but his public support was strong. The 33-year-old is now caught off guard after the rescue deal failed. The DP World Tour has offered him a clear path forward through his U.S. Open win. A five-year exemption resulted from that victory, yet one year was subtracted for every season he skipped membership. This means November 16 is his last chance to utilize that exemption for the 2026-27 season. Missing the deadline means he must depend on sponsor invitations to compete. An invitation to the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa has already been accepted by him. A Shift in the Game High-profile players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton are expected to join the European circuit regularly. Television viewership would receive a particularly notable boost from DeChambeau’s arrival. He faces a hard deadline to join the DP World Tour after his LIV Golf exit. Before liquidation concludes, the league faces an effectively doomed future unless an investor provides substantial funding. That scenario remains exceptionally unlikely. Options Run Dry Richard Bland, another LIV member, admitted he was surprised by the breakdown of the rescue agreement. Bland said, “Obviously it has left me a little bit up in the air. I don’t really have a huge amount of options outside of LIV.” DeChambeau faces a similar reality with fewer years of eligibility left. He might play a little bit in Asia, but he will cross that bridge when he comes to it next year. item.title: Top 2027 recruit Ashley Maccalla commits to Rutgers
item.description: Top 2027 recruit Ashley MacCalla has committed to Rutgers over programs including Oklahoma, Miami and Cal. The 5-10 guard from Middletown (NY) St. James Performance Academy was one of the biggest stockrisers of the summer. “My biggest strength is that every time I step on a court, I’m one of the most athletic girls on the court,” she said. “I really take advantage of it, whether it’s on defense or offense, I’m the type of girl that plays in transition. I don’t really care about highlights or anything like that. I do what my team needs to win, whether that’s just playing defense, getting steals, getting blocks, or pushing in transition. I’m one of those girls that a coach will love to coach, because I don’t really care about the highlight reel and stuff like that. I just want to do what the team needs to do to win.” Rutgers was one of the more recent teams to enter her recruitment, but her relationships with the staff were central. “Rutgers has been on me a lot too, just because they’re literally an hour away from me,” she previously told Rivals. “It’s been really good. Coach G[ary Redus] met most of my family. He was recruiting me at LSU, so I talked to him a lot. I also talk a lot with Lauren Hansen. She used to play for Exodus and she coaches for Exodus for a little bit too, so I already had that bond with her and it’s great talking to them. My parents love him and he’s a great guy. He loves to talk. Campus is beautiful too.” There were several factors that went into her decision. “A connection with the coaches,” she said of important factors. “I’d say play style, like how I’d fit in the system and making sure I get a good opportunity to play. I also have an older sister and I want to make sure that she’s able to come with me. Also somewhere that I can develop. I want to make it to the league.”

item.title: Swans boss Matos defends Stamenic over red card
item.description: Swansea had been the more threatening side at Birmingham until Marko Stamenic (right) was sent off [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Vitor Matos has defended Marko Stamenic after the midfielder was sent off during Swansea City's defeat at Birmingham City. Stamenic saw red in the 26th minute for a heavy challenge on Ethan Laird. Birmingham seized the initiative after Stamenic's early exit, with Jay Stansfield swiftly putting the Blues ahead and then netting a late winner after Swansea levelled in the second half. Matos suggested Stamenic should not have been dismissed because he played the ball rather than former Swansea loanee Laird. "I cannot change what the referee decided," said the Swansea head coach. "I think what happened in that situation was that Marko touched the ball. He tackled the ball with the first foot, he tackled the ball with the second foot. "There's no contact between the two players, so then it's the judgement of the ref if that's a red or not. It's up to him not me." Birmingham beat 10-man Swansea to go top of table Stamenic faces a three-match ban after the first sending off of his Swansea career, with Birmingham boss Chris Davies describing the red card incident as "a poor challenge". Unless Swansea launch a successful appeal, New Zealand player Stamenic will miss games against West Brom, Middlesbrough and Cardiff City after the upcoming international break. "I am here already [in English football] for a good amount of time - I was here before," Matos added. "I saw so many challenges worse than this in the last game. Some of these challenges end up with players injured. It's just harsh when we have this challenge and then there's a red card. "It's for the refs to judge and try to find an agreement on where the line is." When asked about what happened, Matos said: "The ref brought over two [cigarette] lighters [to the fourth official]. "It's more than clear that it is not acceptable. Let's see what happens. Of course it's not right." Nevertheless, the Matos insisted he was "not here to give excuses" after Swansea dropped to sixth in the Championship having been beaten for the fourth time in five matches. The dip in form has come after the Swans lost only one of their first 10 league games this season. "What I am here to say is that with this group of players, with the effort they made and the character they have, we as a club, we will come back," Matos declared. "They will come back and we will go back to our standards."

item.title: NASCAR CEO O’Donnell Bets On YouTube To Fix TV Ratings
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell delivered a blunt truth to the sports world on Friday at Homestead-Miami Speedway. While television ratings for the Cup Series are sagging, the front office refuses to panic. O’Donnell argues that the old metrics do not tell the whole story anymore. He pointed to a 5 percent rise in track admissions and a 12 percent jump in kids under 12 showing up to races, per Newsday . The sport is shifting its focus from the couch to the digital feed, betting that new fans will find the action online first. This is a bold gamble for a league built on tradition, but the numbers back the move. Digital First Strategy O’Donnell knows that a fan in New York or Seattle cannot drive to a race every weekend. The solution is to meet them where they live. “If you’re in New York or you’re in Seattle, and you don’t have a race, what is that entry point?,” O’Donnell said Friday. The answer is short clips and influencer content. To expand the series past its southern origins and enter international markets, the sanctioning body is leveraging YouTube and social media influencers. This strategy acknowledges that the path to a ticket starts with a viral moment on a phone screen. While critics might focus on the drop in broadcast viewership, the CEO sees a different picture. NBC viewership for last week’s Cup race at Martinsville Speedway was down 15 percent from last year, according to Newsday. With an average of just under 2 million viewers, that event became the least-watched non-delayed Cup race on broadcast television. Yet, O’Donnell insists that social impressions increased 34 percent year-over-year. Since 2013, interest levels among adults ages 18 to 34 have reached their peak. The sport is not dying; it is just changing how it breathes. Sponsor Money Talks Money flows to where the attention is, and NASCAR is seeing fresh cash. “Fans are coming out to the racetrack. New brands are investing in the sport like never before,” O’Donnell said. The activation from sponsors around teams and drivers is at a high point not seen in years. This spending power proves that brands believe in the future of the sport even if cable TV numbers dip. “It’s been a long time since you’ve seen the activation from sponsors around our teams and drivers,” O’Donnell noted. The league is also celebrating the addition of Dodge as a fourth manufacturer, adding more competition and buzz to the garage. O’Donnell pushed back hard against the narrative that NASCAR is struggling. “If you compared NASCAR to a new sport that’s just emerging you’d say it’s an incredible success story,” he said. The league has maintained a consistently large television audience across 36 straight weekends. item.description: Motorsport photo Ryo Hirakawa is unsure whether even bold strategic calls will be enough to propel Toyota towards the front in the World Endurance Championship's Monza finale after a difficult qualifying session. Hirakawa admitted the Japanese manufacturer was simply “too slow” after the two TR010 Hybrids ended up 15th and 16th on the grid for Sunday’s race, only ahead of the #15 BMW M Hybrid V8 of Dries Vanthoor. Teams had completed very little representative running on slick tyres across the three practice sessions, with persistent rain on Friday and Saturday morning severely compromising preparations for the Monza 6 Hours. However, Toyota struggled for performance in both wet and dry conditions as the WEC returned to Monza for the first time since the #7 crew's victory in 2023. “It was the same for everyone, no dry running until qualifying, so it was really tricky. Some cars had tested here; we hadn't, so we were just guessing for set-up. We did our best from what we have got, but it's been tough,” Hirakawa said, “Even in the wet, we didn't have a really strong pace.” Asked where he was losing time on track, Hirakawa replied: “In the wet, it was everywhere, even on the straights, but I haven't really seen the performance in the dry. The Gunners boss highlighted the winger's professional transformation during the international break as a key factor in his recent run of explosive form. Arteta praises Madueke's elite mentality Reflecting on the player's recent rise, Arteta said: 'He's a great example for the rest of the group because before the first international break he wasn't playing. item.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton set for blockbuster rematch in final of Paris Masters
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz set up a rematch with US Open conqueror Ben Shelton after he eased into a maiden Paris Masters final with a 6-4 6-4 victory over Casper Ruud . Seven-time grand slam champion Alcaraz lost out in an epic to Shelton at Flushing Meadow in September on his comeback from a four-month lay-off with a wrist injury. The world number three has returned to the winners’ circle twice since his exit in the early hours in New York, but will aim to gain revenge on Shelton and secure another ATP 1000 title on Sunday. US Open runner-up Shelton got the better of home favourite Luca Van Assche by a 5-7 6-3 6-4 score at the start of the day. Carlos Alcaraz set up a meeting with Ben Shelton after a straight set win over Casper Ruud in Paris (Getty) After Shelton’s two-hour-and-17-minute battle, all eyes in Paris were on Alcaraz, who saved two match points to defeat Taylor Fritz on Friday. Ruud narrowly held off Alcaraz in two of his first three service games before the Spaniard broke to move 4-3 up and closed out the first set with a 130mph ace. The second stayed on serve until Alcaraz picked the opportune moment to break to go 5-4 ahead and secured victory inside 97 minutes. It made it eight wins in a row for Alcaraz, who reached an 11th Masters final, but first in Paris. Ben Shelton defeated Luca van Assche to reach Paris Masters Open (Reuters) “This tournament has always been really tough for me. I’ve struggled every time,” Alcaraz said on court. “I’ve come into this part of the season much fresher, hungry, ambitious, excited about coming to the tournaments and stepping on the court, playing matches and competing. I’m just really happy that I made the final.” Shelton, meanwhile, reached the final when he rallied from a break down in the deciding set to beat Van Assche on Saturday. The third-seeded American looked in trouble when the unseeded Frenchman broke his serve for a 3-1 lead in the third set. But Shelton responded by winning the next four games to lead 5-3. “I know there is always going to be some little chance I can execute,” Shelton said. “If I can be brave and keep winning my serve and stick with the guy, I feel there is a small window.”

item.title: Toto Wolff doesn’t think Kimi Antonelli “would have lasted in other teams”
item.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1 is a vicious meat grinder for young talent. If a rookie doesn't perform immediately, there is usually a very short leash before a team principal shows them the door. For Mercedes , taking a massive gamble on teenager Andrea Kimi Antonelli to replace Lewis Hamilton was the ultimate risk. And as team boss Toto Wolff freely admits, there was a dark stretch during the Italian's 2025 rookie campaign where almost any other team on the grid would have pulled the plug. Speaking to Sky Sports F1’s Naomi Schiff and Simon Lazenby following Free Practice 3 at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Wolff took a moment to reflect on exactly how close his newly crowned world champion came to the brink. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Before Antonelli hoisted the 2026 championship trophy in Mexico City, he had to survive a nightmare slump. "What I'm particularly proud of is that I don't think he would have lasted in other teams after an F2 season, which wasn't overwhelming," Wolff confessed on the Sky broadcast. "And this spell of nine races without any points last year." The Mercedes shield When the pressure was at its absolute peak, and critics were questioning the factory seat, the Brackley squad closed ranks. They ignored the outside noise and looked at the telemetry. "We just trusted our data, trusted our feeling about the personality and the potential," Wolff explained. "Because there's so many that came out and said, what a talent. And that wasn't the journey." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Instead of letting the then-19-year-old drown in the immense pressure of the Silver Arrows spotlight, Wolff and his senior leadership team built a psychological fortress around him. "And eventually, you know, he in the car is just delivered absolutely amazingly." The ultimate vindication arrived in Mexico when Antonelli secured the crown. Wolff's patience didn't just save a generational talent from being destroyed by the F1 machine - it built the youngest world champion in F1 history. item.title: Argentina set to go to Cas after Fifa rejects appeals
item.description: Leandro Paredes (centre), Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada all appeared to be involved in a fracas on the pitch after Spain won their World Cup final [Getty Images] The Argentina Football Association says it is planning to apply to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over Fifa rejecting its appeals against punishments handed out to the organisation and midfielder Leandro Paredes. Paredes was given a 10-match ban for his role in on-field clashes following Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. Team-mate Nahuel Molina was given a seven-game ban, with both players being fined $90,000 (£66,000), and while the AFA said Molina's suspension had been reduced to four games by Fifa, the sanctions on Paredes stood. The AFA was fined $321,000 (£235,000) for breaches of the Fifa disciplinary code related to using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. After beating England 2-1 in the World Cup semi-final, several Argentina players held up a banner claiming Argentine sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory. A statement from the AFA said that, as Fifa had upheld the punishments, its next step would be to ask for the reasons for the decisions by world football's governing body before taking the issue to Cas. Following the Word Cup final in July, Argentina players Paredes, Molina and Thiago Almada plus assistant coach Roberto Ayala all appeared to be involved in a fracas on the pitch as Spain celebrated their win. Paredes seemed to push Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and unused substitute Gavi tried to intervene but was forced to the ground by Almada. Fifa later appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess what happened before issuing its sanctions. item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. France and South Africa currently top the two pools, with New Zealand also unbeaten and level on points with the Springboks. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. item.title: Francesco Bagnaia out of Qatar Grand Prix with fractures in right foot
item.description: Motorsport photo Two-time MotoGP world champion Francesco Bagnaia has picked up two fractures in his right foot following his frightening accident during the Qatar Grand Prix sprint race on Saturday. The injury will prevent him from taking part in Sunday's Qatar GP at the very least, with the remainder of the season in doubt as the possibility of surgery is assessed. Bagnaia was pitched high into the air when Gresini Ducati's Fermin Aldeguer lost control under brakes and clattered into him early in the original race. The incident led to a red flag and a completely new race being run - inevitably without Bagnaia. That brought an early end to what had looked his most promising weekend for some time. Read Also: Pecco Bagnaia 'feels like a factory rider again' as he finds form in Qatar Bagnaia was examined by MotoGP medical director Dr Angel Charte, following which a statement was released by Ducati. “Initial medical examinations performed on Pecco Bagnaia at the medical center at the Losail International Circuit have revealed two fractures in his right foot, affecting the fourth and fifth metatarsals," read the statement. Bagnaia was in the thick of the battle before his accident Bagnaia was in the thick of the battle before his accident "The rider will be transferred tonight to Doha Hospital to undergo further tests to determine whether the fractures require surgery,” the Borgo Panigale team concluded. Just two race weekends remain on the MotoGP schedule following the Qatar GP. A gap of two weeks before the Iberian double-header that concludes the season may work in Bagnaia's favour, but at this stage it is possible that his time with Ducati may already be over. Bagnaia, who won two world championships for the team in 2022 and 2023, is approaching the end of two difficult seasons and will race for Aprilia next year. Aldeguer was made to serve a double long lap penalty during the restarted contest.
